formal_benchmark_reason: grouped dataset split and collection release are separate
mechanism: SQLAlchemy 1.4 rejects Placement's use of a ScalarSelect as a FROM expression in the existing online-data-migrations query
repair_template: construct the derived query with the SQLAlchemy 1.4-compatible subquery API while retaining SQLAlchemy 1.3 compatibility

replay.failure_signature: sqlalchemy.exc.ArgumentError: FROM expression, such as a Table or alias() object expected, got <sqlalchemy.sql.selectable.ScalarSelect object at 0x<address>>.

semantic_review.a1_failure: On the unchanged Placement opening-cutoff snapshot, the pre-existing functional status module runs three tests with SQLAlchemy 1.3.23. With 1.4.11, one online-data-migrations test fails with an exclusive ArgumentError because a ScalarSelect is no longer accepted as a FROM expression; the exact maintainer patch restores all three tests.
semantic_review.reviewer_basis: Reviewed the one-pin source opening diff, exact one-file production target diff, cutoff functional tox command, installed-version probes proving SQLAlchemy 1.3.23/1.4.11/1.4.11, patch applicability, and complete three-arm logs. The same three pre-existing functional tests run in every arm; only A1 has the normalized ScalarSelect ArgumentError. The Python 3.8/tox 3 runner, source-era setuptools seed, Cython build constraint, and pip seed are identical across arms and only restore opening-era packaging compatibility.
semantic_review.source_effect: The source opening changes exactly one upper-constraints pin, SQLAlchemy 1.3.23 to 1.4.11; SQLAlchemy 1.4 enforces that FROM elements be tables, aliases, or explicit subqueries rather than ScalarSelect objects.
semantic_review.target_repair: The exact maintainer patch applies to the public opening-cutoff Placement snapshot and changes the production query from alias(as_scalar()) to the explicit subquery() API accepted by both SQLAlchemy 1.3 and 1.4. It changes no test, test selection, or unrelated behavior.
